solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Roman god: he's cruel, unfortunately

indicators.note: something that goes unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters of the phrase before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that some Roman deity is a cruel one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the letters of HE'S CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero Heracles was worshipped by the Romans as a deity under this Latin name.

clue.text: Smoothing the end of the day

definitions.meaning: making level or flat, as a plane does to wood
the close of the day, the time after afternoon and before night

explanation.surface: Ironing things out as a day draws to its close.
explanation.definitionFit: Levelling a surface is making it even; the late part of the day is the period before nightfall.

clue.text: Survived being confined, losing oxygen

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word for confined

parts.note: cooped up means confined in a small space
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Someone came through being shut in and short of air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes one O out of COOPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or get through a difficulty is to have dealt with it successfully, a near synonym of survived.

clue.text: Fall behind lass heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the word for lass is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A girl going north drops back from the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns GAL upward, giving the letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail or straggle behind others is to fail to keep pace.

clue.text: Lager and cider: you'll need an antidote for it!

definitions.meaning: a pub drink of lager mixed with cider, popular in Britain

definitions.text: you'll need an antidote for it
definitions.meaning: a venomous wound from a serpent's fangs calls for antivenom

explanation.surface: A warning that a strong mixed drink will need a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: The British pub drink mixing lager and cider shares its name with a serpent's venomous wound, which needs antivenom.

clue.text: Leave car electrician has failed to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the word for electrician loses its opening letter

parts.note: spark, or sparks, is British slang for an electrician

explanation.surface: An electrician's vehicle won't start, so it has to be left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has failed to start' removes the S from SPARK. Sparks is British slang for an electrician.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a vehicle standing in a place is to station it there.

clue.text: When a car refuels, containers fall over

indicators.note: over signals a turning back, so the pieces for containers and fall are written in reverse

parts.note: pots are containers
to tip is to fall or topple over

explanation.surface: Pots tumble while a car is being refuelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses POTSTIP. 'fall over' looks like one phrase, but only 'fall' gives letters; 'over' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, cars pull into the pits to take on fuel and new tyres during a brief halt.

clue.text: Rinse strange sticky substance

indicators.note: strange suggests something altered and odd, so the letters of the word before it are reordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to wash off some odd gummy stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The gummy exudate of pine and other trees is a classic sticky material.

clue.text: Retain possession of stronghold

definitions.meaning: to continue having something rather than give it up
the fortified central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: Holding on to a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding on to something is to not give it away; a castle's main tower is also known by this word.

clue.text: Seating broken by second very large lady

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A bench gives way under a second, rather big, woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges SEATING into GIANTES; 'by' joins it to S.
explanation.definitionFit: A female of enormous size, like the female ogres in fairy tales.

clue.text: Psychological strategy: look out for wild animals

parts.note: mind, as in 'mind the gap', means look out for
game is wild animals hunted for sport or food

explanation.surface: A safari warning to beware of the wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A calculated ploy to manipulate or unsettle an opponent's thinking.

clue.text: Where the litigious will see you after a good battle

indicators.note: after places the phrase for where litigants go behind the letters for a good

parts.words: Where the litigious will see you
parts.note: people fond of lawsuits will meet you before a judge, at law

explanation.surface: Lawsuit-lovers will meet you after a fine fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts IN COURT after A and G. The battle of 1415 was Henry V's famous victory over the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V's 1415 victory over the French is one of England's most famous historic fights.

clue.text: Colour of metal tiger's head

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: a head is the top or start, so only the opening letter of the word for the big cat is used

explanation.surface: Asking what shade a metal tiger's head is.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade or hue, often a pale one, is a synonym for colour.

clue.text: Rodent disease contained by artificial intelligence

indicators.note: contained by means the disease word sits inside the letters for artificial intelligence

parts.note: gout is a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: A computer program is tracking an illness carried by a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: The rodent is a burrowing creature of Central and South America, a cousin of the guinea pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing South American creature related to the guinea pig, so a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Modernised a dud pet, somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests things worked out by unknown means, so the letters of the phrase are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A useless pet has been brought into the present by unknown means.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing something up to date or refreshing it is to make it current, a synonym for modernised.

clue.text: Consequences of one initially minor agreement

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but the answer is used as a mass noun for effects

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word minor only

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: The fallout from a single small deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The effect or influence of an event, used as a mass noun, covers its results.

clue.text: Wow, delightful ornamental feature

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow
nice means pleasing or delightful

explanation.surface: Someone admiring a lovely decorative detail.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is an informal British cry of surprise, much like 'wow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative moulding running along the top of a wall or building is an ornamental architectural feature.

clue.text: Shakespeare, perhaps, is forbidden on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word for forbidden is taken by its sound

parts.note: barred means forbidden or banned

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's work being banned from the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the radio' gives a word sounding like BARRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet; the Bard of Avon is Shakespeare's nickname, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Prevent a former soldier keeping rifle, at first

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the old soldier wraps around a letter

parts.note: vet is short for veteran, a former soldier

indicators.note: at first selects the opening letter of the word rifle

explanation.surface: An ex-serviceman with a gun stops something happening.
explanation.walkthrough: VET is the US-style short form of veteran. 'keeping' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward off or stop something from happening is to forestall it.

clue.text: Redesign secure HQ where the PM stays sometimes

indicators.note: redesign means to recast in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to remodel a secure headquarters used by the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redesign' rearranges SECURE HQ. The answer is the British Prime Minister's official country house in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The country house in Buckinghamshire is the official weekend retreat of Britain's Prime Minister.

clue.text: Overturn unexpected result

definitions.meaning: to knock over or capsize something
a surprise defeat of a favourite, as in sport

explanation.surface: A reversal producing a surprise outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking something over and a shock sporting defeat share this one word.

clue.text: Try out underground piece of laboratory apparatus

parts.note: to test something is to try it out
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Trialling some lab equipment on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim glass cylinder closed at one end, used by chemists to hold samples.

clue.text: Observe affirmative response, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for yes is taken by its sound

parts.note: aye is an old or dialect word for yes, used in voting

explanation.surface: Watching someone say yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch or look at something closely, as in 'eyeing up' a rival.

clue.text: Cut legs when retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word for legs is reversed

parts.note: pins is informal slang for legs

explanation.surface: Someone's legs got cut as they backed away.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick stroke of scissors is a small cut.

clue.text: Attractive man's bit of jewellery

definitions.meaning: slang for a handsome, sexually attractive man
a small earring or decorative knob fixed through the skin

explanation.surface: A handsome man's earring.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunk is slangily called by this word, which also names a small earring.

clue.text: The current decade represented in tweets

indicators.note: represented is read as re-presented, laid out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: This decade is captured in social media posts.
explanation.definitionFit: The years 2020 to 2029 are the decade the clue was written in.
